answer.rationale: Competitive price-cut pressure creates acute churn risk, but memory_73 and exp_73 clearly show targeted promotional pricing is unsustainable—it acquires price-sensitive cohorts with -12% 30-day retention and poor renewal economics. That path violates the primary objective. Instead, leverage three proven vectors: (1) activation_messaging (memory_91) improves week-one engagement and first meaningful action—directly countering churn by deepening product stickiness; (2) simplify_onboarding (memory_86, memory_31) lifts early adoption and reduces friction during vulnerable early windows; (3) referral_incentive (memory_57) scales qualified revenue from established, retained accounts without harming retention. A standard experiment combining activation messaging with onboarding simplification targets the root of SMB churn—low product adoption and perceived value—rather than competing on price. This preserves margin, targets durable behavioral change, and avoids the renewal-cycle cliff that discounting creates. Enterprise-sales-assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to SMB churn. The strategy holds uncertainty: messaging and onboarding improvements may take 2–3 weeks to show measurable churn impact, so a parallel light referral-incentive offer to established customers provides immediate revenue lever without acquisition risk.
